about: Behaviour settings for data_generator.py: every number that shapes the generated data. Each setting has a 'description' and a 'value'; the generator reads only the values. Every number is an assumption, not a measured fact. Shares and probabilities are between 0 and 1 (0.30 = 30%). Weights are relative likelihoods: only the ratios matter, and the chance of an option is its weight divided by the sum of the weights. docs/data_generation.md explains the math. To try other settings without editing this file, point CARTON_CAPS_GENERATOR_SETTINGS at a copy.

dirty_data_rate.description: Share of purchase and referral rows deliberately corrupted so the pipeline's quality checks have something to catch. 0.01 = 1% of rows, with at least 2 rows of each issue type. Set to 0 for clean data.

activity_segments.description: Every user is put in one segment, which sets how often they buy. share = fraction of users in the segment (the four add up to 1). purchase_rate = purchases per active day relative to a light user (heavy 8 = buys 8x as often as a light user). Inactive users sign up but never scan a receipt.

monthly_churn.description: Chance that a user who is still buying stops for good during a given month, checked every 30 days from signup. Benchmarks: consumer subscriptions lose 5-10% a month (about 6.5% for B2C), replenishment products such as groceries under 4%, the best businesses under 3%. After a year this leaves about 78% of heavy, 61% of regular and 37% of light users buying (0.98^12, 0.96^12, 0.92^12).

referred_churn_multiplier.description: Referred users' monthly churn is multiplied by this. 0.75 = they churn 25% less (1.5% heavy, 3% regular, 6% light).

first_purchase_within_days.description: Every user who buys makes a first purchase at a random moment within this many days of signing up. It is the referral program's 'qualifying action'.

category_preferences.description: Weights for picking a product category, by user type. A parent's weights add up to 5.7, so a parent picks Breakfast 1.4 / 5.7 = 25% of the time and Pantry 0.9 / 5.7 = 16%.

quantity_weights.description: Weights for how many units are bought in one purchase, by user type (keys are the number of units). These add up to 100, so they read as percentages: a parent buys 1 unit 60% of the time. Teachers stock classrooms; supporters (grandparents, neighbours) mostly buy one item.

promo_chance.description: Probability that a single purchase is on promotion: 30% for a bargain hunter, 5% for everyone else. How many users are bargain hunters depends on district income (districts.income_levels).

promo_discounts.description: A promotion takes one of these off the list price, each equally likely (10%, 20% or 30% off).

income_levels.description: A school district is the school's city and state; each gets an income level. share = fraction of districts at that level (adds up to 1). median_income_range = the district's median household income is drawn uniformly between these dollar amounts, rounded to $1,000. bargain_hunter_share = fraction of the district's users who are bargain hunters. price_power tilts which product is picked within a category, weight = price ^ price_power: +1 makes an $8 product twice as likely as a $4 one, 0 makes every product equally likely, -1 makes the $4 product twice as likely.

weekend_weight.description: A Saturday or Sunday is this many times as busy as a weekday (weekdays count as 1.0). A day's busyness = weekend weight x month weight x event multiplier, and a day's chance of being picked is proportional to its busyness.

month_weights.description: Busyness by month, where 1.00 is an ordinary month: a January lull, a spring fundraising push in March, a summer dip in June and July, and back to school in August and September.

hour_weights_weekday.description: Weights for the hour of day on a weekday, once the day is picked. Keys are the hour on a 24-hour clock ("00" = midnight to 1am, "17" = 5pm to 6pm). Peaks at lunch and after work; nights near zero. Signup times use this curve too.

hour_weights_weekend.description: Weights for the hour of day on a Saturday or Sunday. Peaks in late morning (11am).

events.description: Holidays and events. first_day and last_day are inclusive. demand_multiplier multiplies those days' busyness (1.15 = 15% busier, 0.35 = 65% quieter). boosted_categories sell more on those days: their category weight is multiplied by event_category_boost.

event_category_boost.description: An event's boosted categories are this many times as likely to be picked on that event's days (1.6 = 60% more likely).

referred_signup_share.description: Chance that a new signup came through a referral. It rises in a straight line from first_signup (the first signup of the period) to last_signup (the last), because more users are around to refer people as the app grows (viral growth). Halfway through it is 20%.

referrer_tiers.description: Every user gets a referrer tier. organic_share and referred_share = fraction of organic users and of referred users in the tier (each adds up to 1; referred users refer a bit more). win_weight = how likely this referrer is to be the one who brought in a new referred user, relative to a casual referrer (0 = never refers). invite_volume = how many invites that don't convert this tier sends, relative to the other tiers (the total number of invites is set by n).

teacher_champion_multiplier.description: Teachers reach many parents, so their chance of being a champion is multiplied by this (3 = three times as likely).

invite_volume_sigma.description: Spread of invite volume within a tier. Each referrer's volume is multiplied by a lognormal factor with median 1 and this sigma; with 0.6, about two-thirds of referrers land between 0.55x and 1.8x their tier's volume (e^-0.6 and e^+0.6).

referrer_ready_days.description: Days after joining before a user can refer anyone (they try the app first), drawn uniformly between min and max.

referrer_recency_days.description: Enthusiasm fades. When a new user's referrer is picked, each candidate's win weight is multiplied by referrer_recency_floor + e^(-days since they could start referring / this). With 120 days and a floor of 0.25, that is 1.25 on day one, 0.62 after 120 days and 0.30 after a year.

referrer_recency_floor.description: The lowest the enthusiasm multiplier above can fall to.

same_school_referral_share.description: Chance that a referred user's referrer is from their own school. If nobody at the school can refer yet, someone from another school is used.

invite_delay_mean_days.description: Invites that never convert go out this many days after the referrer can start referring, on average (exponential: most in the first couple of months, a few much later).

click_delay.description: Invites that convert: hours from invite to click. Lognormal with this median and sigma (about two-thirds of clicks between median x e^-sigma and median x e^+sigma: 2.2 to 16 hours), capped at max_hours (a week).

signup_delay.description: Invites that convert: hours from click to signup. Lognormal with this median and sigma, capped just under attribution_window_hours.

attribution_window_hours.description: Rules PDF: the referral code must be used within this many hours of installing the app.

click_rate_unconverted.description: Chance that an invite that never converts was still clicked, by referrer tier. Personal invites (casual) get clicked more often than mass invites (champion).

multi_touch_share.description: Fraction of users who joined through a referral that had been invited earlier by someone else (an 'assist'; credit goes to the invite they used).

reinvite_share.description: Fraction of invites that never convert which go to an address that had already been invited.

invitee_email_domains.description: Weights for the email domain of people who were invited but never joined. They add up to 100, so they read as percentages.
